headline: Insilico Medicine's Abu Dhabi team says AI helped it design molecules that destroy a blood cancer protein, though they are years from patients.
score_reason: Early-stage lead compounds from one company, reported through an interview by one outlet; the speed claims are the company's own.
importance_line: Patients with certain leukaemias and lymphomas get another distant candidate, the UAE gets a marker of its drug-discovery ambitions, and Insilico gets a third AI-found compound this year, but the molecules have not yet passed the tests needed to enter clinical trials.
summary: The National reports that researchers at Insilico Medicine, a clinical-stage biotech with a laboratory in Abu Dhabi's Masdar City, used the company's AI platforms to design PROTACs, two-ended molecules that drag a target protein to the cell's disposal machinery, against Bruton's tyrosine kinase, a protein that drives some leukaemias and lymphomas, with details published in the Journal of Medicinal Chemistry. The company calls them "lead compounds" because the tests needed to enter clinical trials are not complete, and its chemist Ahmad Alghaith said the hope of AI is that it will "increase the success rate, reduce time spent and reduce costs" in a field where nine of ten drugs reaching human testing fail.
